title: Handoff choreography for host lifecycle to preserve throughput during drains and upgrades
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem: Scheduled and unplanned host drains during upgrades or maintenance currently cause transient throughput degradation for tenants on Dedicated pools. Simple sequential drains create token-burst latency spikes and cache cold-starts that violate per-customer throughput contracts.

Goal: Implement a host handoff choreography layer that coordinates gradual traffic handover, KV cache prewarm, and autoscaler-aligned buffer allocations so drains and upgrades occur without breaching throughput guarantees. The feature must integrate with existing autoscaling policies, reservation buckets, and rollout controls, and provide observability + runbook hooks for SRE and solutions engineers.
comments: 2025-11-03 - Kickoff: scoped core behavior, stakeholders: Runtime (Marco), Autoscale (Priya), Console (Samira), SRE (Diego).
2025-11-05 - Spike completed: prototype of prewarm protocol (http://confluence.redwood/handshake-prewarm). Observed 40-60% reduction in p95 token latency during test drains on a 64-GPU pool.

2025-11-07 - Design review: decided to avoid centralized coordinator to reduce blast radius; will use lease-based decentralized handoff with leader election per maintenance window. Trade-off: complexity vs. resilience. (Design doc: http://confluence.redwood/host-handoff-choreography).
2025-11-09 - PR opened for runtime hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2124. Contains drain-proxy shim and metrics emission for handoff phases.
2025-11-11 - UX sync: Console team added a maintenance timeline UI hook; added labels to API for ‘handoff-window’ and ‘buffer-size’.
2025-11-12 - Integration test flake found: race when multiple hosts attempt prewarm for the same shard. Added a backoff + dedupe token in PR 2130.
Follow-ups: add e2e canary across three dedicated pools, update runbook, and schedule SRE tabletop before GA rollout.
acceptance_criteria: When a host enters a scheduled drain, traffic to its active shards is shifted according to a staged window such that per-tenant throughput never drops below 95% of the SLA baseline for more than 15s.
KV cache prewarm runs on candidate targets prior to accepting traffic; measured cold-start token cost reduction >= 30% in staged canary.
System emits 'handoff_phase' metrics (candidate, prewarm, accept, finalize) and Console shows per-pool timeline visualization.
Feature integrates with autoscaler: reserved buffer is honored and autoscaler does not reclaim buffer capacity during handoff windows.
SRE runbook updated and tabletop run completed with no critical gaps.
tasks: Implement decentralized lease protocol for handoff coordination in runtime (runtime team).
Add prewarm API and background worker to populate KV cache on target hosts.
Expose handoff controls in Console (timeline, buffer size, emergency abort).
Add metrics and alerts for handoff phase durations and per-tenant throughput deltas.
Create e2e canary that simulates upgrades on 3 dedicated pools and validates acceptance criteria.
Update autoscaler to respect handoff-reserved buffers and expose policy toggles.
Rollout plan: canary -> phasing -> GA with customer communication templates.
decision_log: Use decentralized, lease-based choreography rather than single orchestrator to improve availability and simplify maintenance-window ownership.
Introduce a configurable buffer reservation (default 10% of pool) that the autoscaler cannot drain while a handoff window is active.
Prewarm will be best-effort with dedupe tokens to avoid redundant cache loads; if prewarm fails, system will fail-safe to conservative staged traffic shift.
Expose an emergency abort in Console that immediately reverses handoff and signals SRE for manual intervention.
risk_mitigation: Canary on non-production fleets first and set strict abort thresholds for p99 increase.
Add telemetry to detect duplicate prewarm and throttling to avoid pressure on origin hosts.
Limit default buffer size and allow account-level overrides to prevent cost/regression for low-tier customers.
Coordinate rollout with Sales/CS for customers with strict throughput contracts.
